5672.title: [v4] Deprecate `res.clearCookie` accepting `options.maxAge` and `options.expires`
5672.author: jonchurch
5672.body:
closes https://github.com/expressjs/express/issues/5640

Adds a deprecation notice when users pass a truthy value in `options` for `maxAge` or `expires` when calling `res.clearCookie(name, options)`.

example:
> res.clearCookie: Passing "options.maxAge" is deprecated and should be removed. Starting with the next major release of Express, this option will be ignored, as res.clearCookie will automatically set cookies to expire immediately. Please update your code to omit this option.

Related #4852

5792.title: Ignore `expires` and `maxAge` in `res.clearCookie()`
5792.author: jonchurch
5792.body:
Opened a new PR for this, supersedes https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/4852

closes https://github.com/expressjs/express/issues/4851

The PR overrides any expires value set, and explicitly deletes maxAge from the options object.

The reason this is needed is that `res.cookie()` will set a relative `expires` value if it sees a `maxAge` value in the options.

clearCookie is meant to delete a cookie, but that deletion can be thwarted if you pass a `maxAge` value, by setting an `expires` into the future relative to the `maxAge`

6073.title: response: add support for ETag option in res.sendFile
6073.author: juanarbol
6073.body:
This patch introduces the ability to control the ETag generation through the `res.sendFile` function. Specifically, the ETag option is wired to the application's configuration, allowing it to be enabled or disabled based on the app's settings.

Fixes: https://github.com/expressjs/express/issues/2294

941.title: Remove 'app' argument to creating a new router
941.author: defunctzombie
941.body:
If the app is not required for Router creation, then users can create disjoint routes and use them at different times in the middleware chain. It could also aid in more dynamic route creation disjoint from knowing the app.

Currently the 'app' parameter is used only to detect strict and case sensitive routes which could instead be arguments to the router creation.

2215.title: remove/opt-out of `qs` module
2215.author: jonathanong
2215.body: looking through `qs`'s issues, it seems like there isn't even a consensus on how nested query string parsing should be. we should either remove it, opt out of it, or create semantics everyone could agree on and redo the `qs` module

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body: This is about the `req.query`, is that right?

comments.author: jonathanong
comments.body: yeah

comments.author: jonathanong
comments.body: maybe do an option like `app.querystring = require('qs')` or something

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body: OK, just checking :) `req.query` should really be a getter anyway, instead of some weird automatic middleware. Also, `querystring` module in core sucks because it's also unpredictable: sometimes a value is a string and sometimes it's an array.

comments.author: jonathanong
comments.body: really? i thought it was always a string. i thought `qs` was giving me all the different ttypes

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body: no, even core is broken. `?foo=bar&foo=baz` will give `['bar', 'baz']` in code. This is fine, but you still have to test if it is an array or not. A proper interface to query values would be `req.query.get('foo')` which would give first occurrence and `req.query.all('foo')` will give you an array of all (and if only a single value, just a one element array). This would thus guarantee the type you're getting.

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body: It's also what like all the other languages like to do.

comments.author: jonathanong
comments.body: ohhh. i guess i'd be down for a module like that, except it should have a convenience method to return an object. the object should probably return only strings as default and optionally do the nested/array/type inferencing magic

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body: Right. I can see the convenience method taking an option to return all values as strings only (so first value when there are multiple), all as arrays, or the mixed format. Then people will know if they asked for the mixed, they'll know what kind of checking they need to be doing or whatever.

comments.author: defunctzombie
comments.body:
We should be providing a query string module but optionally allowing the user to bring their own (maybe via setting when creating the app or something)

We can do what @jonathanong suggested or optionally think about

``` js
var app = express({ qs: my_qs });
```

I know we haven't passed options to express like this before but maybe it could work.

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body:
Right. I see many different things going on here:
1. `req.query` should be a getter instead of added by middleware. This would be nice in that you only have to parse the query if you want it, instead of always without a choice.
2. We need to have some better default parsing, probably something where users don't get into trouble with just slapping crap around (because they didn't realize a value could be an array, object, or what-have-you).
3. Let people override this, especially important if it becomes a getter.

We have setting stuff already with `app.set('trust proxy', val)`, `app.set('view engine',  val)`, etc. I think all the settings should be in the same location, so we can either add the `qs` parser there, or move all that stuff into the `express` constructor (but not have them mixed where some are one way and some are another way).

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body: There is now a commit on the 4.7 branch that implements this. A user can opt-out of parsing with `app.disable('query parser')`, change it to not use `qs` with `app.set('query parser', 'simple')`, or provide their very own whatever they want parser with `app.set('query parser', fn)`.

3361.title: Consider disabling extended query string parsing by default
3361.author: randomdross
3361.body:
I created a simple browser-based XSS filter test app here:
http://xss.untrusted.com/xss?id=aaa&id=bbb
This is page is simple enough that pretty much any filter bypass bug present here would be legitimate.  That is, the identified bypass condition would have to be in-scope as an issue for the filter to defend against.

Masato Kinugawa was able to bypass the IE / Edge XSS filter using the following trick:
http://xss.untrusted.com/xss?id[0]=%3Cscript/&id[1]=/src=//html5sec.org/test.js%3E%3C/script%3E
This relies on the extended query string parsing that is enabled by default in express.

I was able to fix my test app by manually disabling the extended query string parsing:
app.set('query parser', 'simple');

While it's certainly not the responsibility of express to make the IE / Edge XSS Filter's job any easier, disabling the extended query parsing by default would be one way to solve this issue for the filter.

Adam Baldwin alerted me to this issue and FWIW he is also in favor of changing the default query parser to 'simple': https://twitter.com/adam_baldwin/status/884633562292428800

Disclosure: Though I'm currently employed by Google, in a previous life I worked at Microsoft developing the IE / Edge XSS Filter.

comments.author: dougwilson
comments.body:
Yes, the plan is to disable by default in Express 5.0. You can view the 5.0 plan here: https://github.com/expressjs/express/pull/2237

> Make query parser option default to 'simple'

I hope this helps! I even updated the plan to reference this issues in the check list for that entry, since there wasn't a specific issue before that I recall, just discussions.

comments.body: Oh that's awesome!  Thank you Doug!

comments.body: And the `body-parser` module has the same thing, which is also being defaulted off in it's 2.0 release.
